params.note: quick test: stag round 2, antlers ignore the top view

method: blockout (19 parts from parts.json) grown 0.0 mm, trimmed to the outlines (8.76 mm voxels), smoothed; kept 1 of 5 mesh pieces; built on a finer grid and joined on: antler beam, brow tine, upper tine, tail, front leg, hind leg fwd, hind leg back
warnings: front and mirrored back outlines overlap only 0.78, even lined up as well as they can be: pose differs between views
views ignored for parts they disagree with (one view would have cut deep into a part the others draw whole): ear: top

a loose piece (0.9% of the model) came off and was dropped: a part (often a tail, ear or horn) joins the body only where trimming cuts it; start it inside the part it grows from, and build a thin tail, strand or leg as a chain (thin chains are built on a finer grid, with whatever hangs from them)

kept untrimmed, because trimming to the outlines would have removed most of them (they are off their drawn place; move them onto it in parts-on-refs.png): hind hoof fwd outer, hind hoof fwd inner, hind hoof back outer, hind hoof back inner, brow tine, upper tine
